APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF MARCH 5, 2019

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:03 pm

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Jerry Velasco, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Velasco  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.4.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at
  approximately 6:04 p.m.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:09 p.m.

  Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla reported out of Closed Session with
  respect to Items 4.1 through 4.4.

  4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel Regarding Anticipated Litigation – One (1)
  Matter.

  General update, no final action
   City Council Meeting Minutes of March 5, 2019

  4.2  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel to Discuss Matter of Existing Litigation – City of
  Temple City, et al. vs. GSC Holding Group, LLC, et al. LASC Case No.
  19STCP00254.

  General update, no final action

  4.3  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation Regarding the Following
  Matter: El Rovia vs. City of El Monte, Los Angeles Superior Court Case No.
  BS172209.

  Agreed to allow the City Attorney to associate with Demetriou, Del Guercio
  Law Firm for purposes of defending the initiated appeal in the subject
  litigation.

  4.4  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation: Eric A. Walterscheid vs. City
  of El Monte, Los Angeles Superior Court, Case No. BC495445.

  General update, no final action

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Velasco  5-0

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS
  (Commencing at 6:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed
  Session/Short Recess)

5.  INVOCATION:  Chaplain Daisy Swan, Calvary Assembly of God Church. Present

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  Angelique Vasquez, 5th Grader from Cherrylee School. Enjoys
  Cheerleading. Present

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS:

  7.1  Presentation by the City Council to Angelique Vasquez from Cherrylee School for
  Leading the Pledge of Allegiance. Present

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any

  2
   City Council Meeting Minutes of March 5, 2019

member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
agenda.

Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

Cheryl Gilera – Manger for El Monte Library. I just wanted to share with everyone about
the different programs that we are offering this month and for the next couple of months.
We actually have series of programs that we are offering to older adults. On Friday,
March 8th we are having Protecting Yourself Against Financial Fraud Workshop that may
be of interest to members of the community. Also every month we are offering games
and conversation in the afternoon for older adults that will be Fridays, March 22nd, April
26th, and May 24th from 1:30 pm to 3:30 pm. Also for children we’ve got Let’s Make
Books that will take place on Saturday, May 23rd from 2:00 pm to 3:30 pm and it is for
children who are interested in making books.

Kimberly Saavath – I used to be an employee here but I am South El Monte now. I
wanted to know what the Council thought about me running a Farmer’s Market for our
City.

Cosme Jimenez – Marijuana is on the Consent Calendar being that it is so critical it
shouldn’t be on the Consent Calendar. New Councilmembers congratulations to those
coming on Board.  Mayor I would like to see more participation from the
Councilmembers. Listen to the people you have to listen you got elected to listen to the
people and you are not listening to them and their concerns.

Edward Barrera – As part of the celebration for Women’s History Month Senator Susan
Rubio and Assemblywoman Blanca Rubio have sponsored a one day seminar for young
women from the ages of 14 to 18 on Saturday March 23rd and the topics to be discussed
will be: Financial Literacy; Etiquette; Healthy Relationships and Social Media. It is free
to any young woman who wishes to come but you do have to RSVP.

Ken Meng – I want to say I love people. It is not easy when we meet together when we
get together because there is something behind. Our family goes to church every
Sunday I am honored to introduce my family here because I love them and I know all my
family loves the society and the community we are willing to serve the community. We
know love is the most important in our life that is why we come here because we know
what is good and what is bad.

David Lim – A couple of weeks ago I spoke to Mr. Jerry about a zoning problem because
my neighborhood’s zoning changed from R-2 to R-3. The City Council failed to report to
the County, State and Federal so actually I don’t even know if the changing of the zoning
is correct. The zoning changed to R-3 zone but when I bought the property it was R-2
zone. The County tells me that it is one zone and the City tells me that it is another zone.
Who is responsible for informing the County of the zoning change?

12.  CONSENT CALENDAR:

  All matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine in nature and
  may be enacted by one motion approving the recommendation listed on the Agenda.
  One or more items may be removed from the Consent Calendar so that they may be
  discussed, considered and voted upon individually by the Council. A matter may be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and taken up separately by way of a seconded
  motion of any member of the Council with the approval of a majority of the Council
  quorum.

Diane Cheung – I am so impressed you have an opening prayer talking about
God and making good decisions for the City and I am grateful for your good
intentions. I know you have good intentions to help your City to be more
prosperous. You have to look for righteousness and then your City will be
prosperous but if you look for money first your City is going to be poor.

Ken Meng – President of Greater Los Angeles Committee Alliance. We are
opposing the projects to plant marijuana in El Monte because these are big
projects and it will cause a lot of trouble for the society. We just want for you to
listen it is not good.

Sam Meng – The City of El Monte should set an example to the community and
their children to not put money on income in front of public safety and health.

Sharon Liao – You pass marijuana projects under nursery license and
regulations. Nursery license and regulations are controlled by USDA by Federal
Government. But for Federal Government marijuana is still number one drug as
heroin. So I question how Federal Government employees can inspect the plan
without being against the law. Growing indoor plans require heat and water. As
an El Monte resident I saw students transfer to other schools because of power
cuts. Please ban the projects you have approved.

Haul Wong – As you know marijuana becomes a controversial issue. You have
approved marijuana facilities in El Monte and they are for medical use. The only
concern for the City is tax revenue and the only concern for the facility is to make
money only. I strongly oppose marijuana for entertainment use.

Zig Jiang – Some people and the applicants argue that it is the stigma and
misunderstanding of the medical marijuana opposition of cannabis facilities in our
community and it is an Asian culture well that is not true. I know many non-Asian
friends who share the same concerns. Most of the signatures on the 4400
Temple City Boulevard Referendum around 400 where from Latino families,
Caucasian families and others only about 2,000 were from Asian families. I fully
understand that the application is intended for producing medicinal cannabis and
not for recreational marijuana but I still am highly concerned for the following
concerns: the close proximity to schools and homes, the land where the facilities
are being built is contaminated, the huge water and power use. I would also like
to share some research facts that show the impact of medical cannabis to the
community.

Alan Zhong – You all know what is going on. I strongly oppose these two
marijuana facilities and other such projects in the City of El Monte. We the hard
working citizens and the taxpayers have every right to decide what is good or
bad for our City.

Ron Williams –Wwe are here discussing and issue that should not be discussed.
There is no unrenderable safe lever or use of cannabis. I don’t want this to be
known as a town that is developing a new industry of derogatory influence.

Joe Meng – I think it is disappointing that we are here again talking about the
same issue that has come before us over and over again with a community that
doesn’t support it. I think it is very disappointing that we were able to collect the
amount of signatures needed and a lot more for the referendum and I think it is a
disgrace for a community to have to request a large amount of money up front in
order to start a business.

  don’t even know how it got this far. I represent New Hope Community Church
  which has been a church in the community for over 50 years and I know

  Chiff Chih – As you know marijuana becomes a controversial issue. You have
  approved marijuana facilities in El Monte and they are for medical use. The only

  Kewei Zhao – As a citizen of the City of El Monte I urge members to vote at least

  Mei Tang – I love El Monte, I love Temple City and I love the City where I live
  here is very peaceful. I oppose this project I do not like marijuana factories set up

  Shun Lian – I am a resident of El Monte and I am not against medical use but I
  am against marijuana facilities in resident area. As everyone knows in Southern
  California we are short of water grow a lot of marijuana and it will need a lot of
  water and this will cause the residents to have less water. Growing marijuana
  will also use more power and this will impact the regular electric City use. This
  will also affect the community safety we need a quiet and peaceful community in
  El Monte. So we strongly oppose any marijuana facility in El Monte.

  Mike Gomez – I want to read a total of 33 States, the District of Columbia, Guam,
  and Puerto Rico have approved a comprehensive public medical marijuana
  cannabis program. I am for medical marijuana. The key word here is medical.
  This is not a dispensary we are not opening any dispensaries.

  There is the ASPCA Mobile they are going to be having on March 6, 8, 12, 13,

  During my participation in these meetings I wanted to bring back that there are
  some really exciting things that have been happening for El Monte. In is

  The City of El Monte is receiving two grants. Thank you to SCAG and again

  I want to share with my colleagues and staff that at the last Alameda Corridor

18E.  Councilwoman Morales

  I would like to continue on that same spirit of celebrating women the last couple
